change_class_rationale: Documentation and planning artifact change only. Adds j76-j90 locale-pack overlay user journeys, schemas, per-service implementation plan slices, integration plans, README files, a bounded delivery report, and this evidence record. No ADR, standard, existing PRD, or existing ARCHITECTURE.md file was intentionally edited.
reviewer: codex-leader self-review with generated artifact validation
review_mode: artifact-floor validation plus multispectrum scorecard before Oya VCS done/promote

F1_linus.headline: The slice uses one repeatable artifact grammar per journey and avoids bespoke layouts; service IPs are role-specific but structurally uniform.

F2_hyperscaler.headline: Coverage is broad enough for pack-overlay reasoning without pretending every pack touches all services; 174 concrete service slices replace vague platform claims.

F3_adversarial.headline: Validation attacked common false greens: missing files, short files, invalid schemas, forbidden placeholders, anonymous services, and over-word report.

F4_ergonomic.headline: Each pack has a README, UX flow, handshake, test plan, schema, and role-specific IP slices so downstream implementers can start from local context.

F5_quality.headline: Generated docs meet line floors, schemas parse, and the report word count is bounded at 197 words.

F6_alternatives.headline: Selected additive locale-pack overlays over ADR edits, global service rewrites, or a single generic compliance journey because the brief required non-colliding j76-j90 artifacts.
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Additive per-pack journey overlays satisfy the brief while preserving protected source boundaries and future implementation optionality.
rejected_reasons: Generic journey would lose regulator-specific deadlines and conflicts
Service-only notes would miss UX, handshake, schema, and test surfaces

F7_security.headline: Artifacts model Cedar policy checks, tenant boundaries, BYOK disambiguation, audit sealing, and no-secret handling without introducing executable code or credentials.

F8_performance.headline: No runtime code changed; journeys specify async regulator evidence assembly, deadline timers, degraded-mode behavior, and idempotent fanout where latency matters.

F9_compliance.headline: Each journey names pack-specific authority surfaces and conflict patterns; the report captures cross-jurisdiction higher-restriction and residency precedence rules.

F10_reversibility.headline: The slice is additive and path-scoped to j76-j90 plus new IP/report/evidence files; rollback is file deletion or git revert without schema migration.

F11_observability.headline: Journeys consistently route evidence through audit-chain, compliance, workflow timers, regulator bundles, and ADR-0263-style event classes.

F13_migration.headline: New j76-j90 directories fill the requested range without editing j01-j75 or j91-j150 surfaces and without changing public contracts.

M1_challenge_assumption.headline: The change does not claim runtime completion; it authors the requested planning and implementation artifacts at the mandated depth.

M2_zoomed_out_fit.headline: The locale-pack work fits the FD-001 pack lane and preserves the masterplan boundary by adding machine-scannable pack-specific overlays.

A1_naming.headline: Journey directories, schema objects, and IP filenames follow jNN-slug and IP-journey-jNN-role naming without introducing anonymous placeholders.

A2_documentation.headline: All required artifact classes are present for all 15 journeys and exceed the line floors.

A3_structure.headline: Artifacts stay in docs/user-journeys and existing flat microservices/<service> directories, matching ADR-0131 layout expectations.

A4_architecture.headline: The pack activation cascade keeps identity, tenancy, consent, workflow, Cedar, audit-chain, and compliance responsibilities separated.

A5_dependency.headline: No new package, SDK, binary, or runtime dependency was added; all changes are text/JSON artifacts.

A6_schema_algorithm.headline: Each pack includes a parseable schema object and handshake algorithm sections for regulator deadline, consent, residency, audit, and conflict-resolution flow.

A7_testing.headline: Every journey has an integration-test-plan.md above the required floor and the slice has an external validation corpus recording counts and failures.
